_what: Declarative watch list for the ternary-leg watchdog (.github/workflows/ternary-leg-watchdog.yml).
_why: Monitoring used to live in a background poller inside an agent session. That dies whenever the session or container stops -- twice on 2026-07-25, once silently for 31 minutes on an unbounded curl -- and a long GPU leg then runs unwatched: a spot preemption is not noticed, nothing resumes it, and the wall clock is lost. This file plus the scheduled workflow move the watch OUT of the session entirely. All state lives in the repo and in GCS, so it survives restarts, and no agent needs to be awake.
_how: The workflow runs on a cron. For each enabled entry it asks GCS three questions: is the leg's result JSON already there (done), is the leg ADVANCING (a live VM whose committed iteration is still climbing), or is it dead/stalled? Only a dead leg is re-dispatched, which resumes from the last committed checkpoint. A per-day relaunch counter in GCS caps runaway re-dispatch, and every outcome is an annotation; a stall or a hit cap also FAILS the job so GitHub's own failure notification fires.
_editing: Set enabled=false when a leg is finished or deliberately parked -- do NOT delete the entry, so the history of what was watched stays legible. The watchdog is a no-op with an empty or all-disabled list.
_required_keys_are_enforced: ONE FACT, ONE PLACE: `_required_run_params` is the single authoritative list and `_required_run_params_note` explains it. `_prefix_keying_params` is retained ONLY as a backward-compatible alias, because a copy of watchdog_validate.py held by another session may still read that key; it is a SUBSET (it lacks use_preequil) and must not be treated as the requirement. The workflow validates the list on every pass and refuses to act on an incomplete entry rather than relaunching the wrong thing.

watch.note: valB_mini reverse leg — the preregistered |dG_fwd + dG_rev| antisymmetry check, still null on all three legs. Its result decides whether the r0 systematic sits in the model/reference data (rescope the calibrator) or in interface substates (change the rescope design first). use_preequil=1 IS THE FIX AND IS ALSO WHAT FWD DID. nr4a3_ternary_fep.py records it verbatim: 'The fix that WORKS is NOT a smaller timestep: relax the fully-interacting physical complex with plain MD BEFORE the alchemy ... where every prior run died at warmup iter 1.' Both 2026-07-25 rev attempts died at warmup iter 1 -- at 2.0 fs (state 1) and at 1.0 fs (state 7) -- confirming empirically that the timestep is not the lever. fwd's prefix is ..._wu1.0_v2pe, and that salt is named for the v2 PRE-EQUILIBRATED setup (SETUP_VER=v2pe is set only by use_preequil=1), so pre-equilibration is not a deviation from fwd: it is what fwd did, which fixes the crash AND preserves comparability for the hysteresis test.

_required_run_params_note: Every parameter the watchdog must REPRODUCE on a relaunch; `_required_run_params` below is the authoritative list. Two classes, both mandatory. (1) PREFIX-KEYING: the spot commit prefix is <seed>_dt<timestep_fs>fs_clig0_wu<warmup_timestep_fs>[_<commit_salt>][_dir<direction>], so omitting one makes the watchdog resume a DIFFERENT trajectory than the one it is watching. (2) NOT prefix-keying but SYSTEM-CHANGING: use_preequil selects whether the alchemy starts from the plain-MD-relaxed physical complex (SETUP_VER=v2pe) or the raw one (v1). CORRECTED 2026-07-25 -- an earlier version of this note claimed pre-equilibration 'only moves coordinates' so 'the particle counts are IDENTICAL' and OpenFE could not catch a v1/v2pe cross-restore. That was never measured and it is FALSE: the prime markers give v1 = 146,020 particles and v2pe = 141,968, because the pre-equilibrated complex is RE-SOLVATED, so assert_multistate_system_equality WOULD reject a cross-restore. Reproducing use_preequil is mandatory for a stronger reason: the setup-cache key carries the version (..._r0__nagl__v1 vs ..._r0__nagl__v2pe), so getting it wrong runs a DIFFERENT SYSTEM, not merely a bad resume. That is what happened: four rev attempts ran the 146,020-particle v1 system against a fwd leg built at 141,968, and all four died at warmup iteration 1. See sections J-J.5 of ternary-lane-guard-audit-2026-07-25.md.
_relaunch_cap_note: max_relaunches_per_day was 8 and that is a HARD BLOCKER at the observed spot preemption rate. Measured 2026-07-25: two consecutive L4 spot VMs on this leg lasted ~30 min and <=62 min (mean ~45 min). Against 26.4 h of remaining MD that is ~35 VM lifetimes, so a cap of 8 would stop the watchdog relaunching on day one and the leg would sit dead with no GPU running and only a CAPPED annotation to show it. Raised to 40. RAISING IT IS SAFE ONLY BECAUSE the crash detector now separates the two cases: a leg that DIED (no VM, no post-mortem -- preemption) is relaunched and resumes from its last committed checkpoint, while a leg that CRASHED (post-mortem newer than its VM) is reaped and explicitly NOT relaunched. So a deterministic failure cannot spin the counter; only preemptions consume it, and each one resumes rather than restarts. Before the crash detector existed, a low cap was the only thing standing between a repeating crash and a runaway.
_provisioning_note: standard (= ON-DEMAND). **AUTHORIZED BY trimcrae 2026-07-25 ~5:30 PM ET**, which is the authorization gpu-ternary-fep-gcp.yml requires: 'Use standard ONLY when explicitly authorized for a time-sensitive one-off, e.g. confirming a single valB leg'. This is that one-off -- the leg gates the entire valB_mini rescope decision. It is a deliberate, recorded reversal of the standing DEFAULT EVERY GPU RUN TO SPOT rule, and it applies to THIS leg only; new work still defaults to spot. The decision (on-demand beats spot for this leg) is UNCHANGED by the corrections in _rate_appendix below -- a slower true per-iteration cost makes the leg longer, which makes preemption-free wall clock worth MORE, not less. TO REVERT: set this back to 'spot'; the switch takes effect on the next relaunch. NB pricing.md still forbids quoting the L4-on-demand figure as a go-forward COST BASIS for the program; spending stranded credit on one gating leg is a different question from pricing the ladder.
_measured_rate:
TWO NUMBERS, MEASURING DIFFERENT THINGS. Use 59 s/iter for any ETA and 56.5 s/iter when talking about MD cost.
  MD cost, in-log, per-iteration, unquantized (iter_timing_profile.awk SEGMENT lines, GH run 30210933840): production is FLAT at 56.2-57.1 s/iter across 600 consecutive production iterations (56.56, 56.22, 56.62, 56.45, 56.38, 57.14 per 100-iteration block). Warmup on the same VM is 47.2 s/iter. THERE IS NO CREEP -- an earlier reading of 'rises 45.3 -> 56.5 then plateaus' was the warmup->production step, not a drift: this VM restored warmup@200 and ran 200->800, so the profile's 600th timing line IS the phase change, which the driver's own 'restore -> warmup@iter 200' line and the GCS census (warmup complete at 800) both confirm independently.
  WALL cost, end-to-end from the GCS commit-marker series: ~59-60 s/iter (production 80 -> 560 across 479 min of VM life = 59.9). The ~6% over the in-log value is COMMIT+UPLOAD overhead -- a ~25 MB .nc/.chk pair to GCS every 40 production iterations, 12 commits over that window, which is the right order for the gap.
  MARKER RATES ARE QUANTIZATION-LIMITED TO ROUGHLY +/-6% EVEN OVER 8-HOUR WINDOWS, because a marker's position is only known to the nearest 40 iterations and the watchdog polls 20-70 min apart. The same series has yielded 48.5, 56.3, 59.9, 66.0 and 70.5 s/iter over different cuts; NONE of those is a slowdown or a speed-up, and the 70.5 was checked against the in-log profile precisely because it looked like one. Quote the in-log value for MD, add the measured commit overhead for wall clock, and never diagnose a rate change from markers alone.
  Warmup and production run the SAME number of MD steps per iteration (OpenFE fixes n_steps once from the PRODUCTION timestep: 2.5 ps time_per_iteration / 2.0 fs = 1250 steps, and rbfe_spot_driver builds the warmup move as a COPY with only .timestep changed), so the 47.2 -> 56.5 step is NOT step count -- production also writes positions every 20 iterations into a growing .nc. That is a 1.2x difference, not the 1.95x originally chased, and it is why the 33.91 s/iter once on record could not be extrapolated: it was a warmup measurement from a DIFFERENT (spot) VM and matches neither phase here.
_leg_targets: warmup_target=800 (ci=8), prod_target=2000 (ci=40) -- read from the driver's own log line, not derived. prod_target=2000 is production_length 5.0 ns / time_per_iteration 2.5 ps. A full leg is therefore ~2800 iterations ~= 40 h of MD at 60.5 s/iter, which is why the on-demand max-run cap was raised 72000s -> 144000s (20 h -> 40 h) in gpu-ternary-fep-gcp.yml: at 20 h EVERY leg needs at least two VMs, and each VM boundary costs 2-4 h of dead wall clock because recovery depends on the watchdog cron (GitHub delivers this repo's crons at ~2-4 h intervals regardless of the requested */15).
_rate_appendix: SUPERSEDED NUMBERS, kept because they stay quotable and CI needs to find copies (CLAUDE.md rule 1.2). (a) '33.91 s/iter' and the derived '106.2 iter/h': a WARMUP measurement from the earlier spot attempts, applied to the whole leg. The true cost is 60.5 s/iter end-to-end -- 1.78x -- so every duration derived from it was ~44% too short. (b) 'the remaining 2704 iterations are ~48 h of calendar on spot vs ~25.5 h un-preempted, so ~23 h saved': built on (a); the un-preempted figure for 2704 iterations at 60.5 s/iter is ~45 h, not 25.5 h. (c) '~2 VM lifetimes instead of ~35' for the 20 h cap: the 20 h cap could never span a ~40 h leg, so it was always >=2 VMs and the comment in gpu-ternary-fep-gcp.yml claiming 20 h 'spans the WHOLE run uninterrupted' was wrong; corrected there and the cap raised to 40 h. (d) 'COST: ~$10 of GCP trial credit': that was one 20 h VM at the old rate estimate. Actual exposure for the whole leg is ~40-46 h of on-demand L4 ~= $30-40 of TRIAL CREDIT, $0 cash, on credit that expires 2026-10-10 and is otherwise stranded. (e) a reading of 'production/280' taken at 8:01 AM 2026-07-26 was reported as ~299 in a status message; the marker series is 80/120/120/200/240/240/280/320 and was monotonic throughout -- there was no regression, the 299 was simply wrong. (f) an ETA of 'Mon 9:30 AM - 12:40 PM ET' derived from (a) is withdrawn; see _eta. (g) '60.5 s/iter', which this file carried for a few hours on 2026-07-26: correct arithmetic over the window available at the time (production 80 -> 320 across 242 min) but a SHORT window, and marker quantization dominates those -- the same series yields 66.0 s/iter and 48.5 s/iter over two other sub-windows. Superseded by 56.5 s/iter, which is the in-log per-iteration plateau and is corroborated to 0.3% by the long-window marker rate (80 -> 440 across 338 min = 56.3 s/iter). Not a measurement error, a window-length error; the lesson is to quote the unquantized in-log value and use markers only to corroborate it. (h) an ETA of 'Mon 3:20 PM - 5:20 PM ET' derived from (g) is withdrawn; see _eta. (i) '~68 iter/h (52.8 s/iter)', which STRATEGY.md's schedule row carried: a WARMUP-window figure from two short baselines (63 min and 190 min), and a fourth value for this one fact -- 33.91, 52.8, 60.5 and 56.5 were all live in the repo at once, which is precisely the failure CLAUDE.md rule 1 exists to stop. Superseded by 56.5 s/iter. That row now POINTS here instead of restating, along with its stale 'warmup/640' position and its '~Mon 8:40 AM' ETA. (j) 'Mon 1:10 PM - 3:10 PM ET', quoted at 11:02 AM: derived from 56.5 s/iter used as a WALL rate, when it is the MD-only rate. Adding the measured ~6% commit+upload overhead gives ~59 s/iter and moves completion ~1.5 h later. (k) a 70.5 s/iter reading over the last 141 min was NOT a slowdown -- it was marker quantization, and the in-log SEGMENT profile (flat 56.2-57.1 s/iter over 600 production iterations) is what established that. Recorded because the check is the point: a 25% apparent slowdown on a billed leg had to be either confirmed or killed with data, not waved off as noise.
_eta: As of 12:39 PM ET Sun 2026-07-26 (watchdog run on VM age 1077 min): production 560/2000, warmup 800/800 COMPLETE, advancing monotonically (320/400/440/520/560), no NaN, no preemption since 6:40 PM Sat.
